newsitem.title: USA: NYSE elects two new directors, re-elects nine.
newsitem.headline: NYSE elects two new directors, re-elects nine.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said two new directors were elected and nine current directors were re-elected to the exchange's board at its annual meeting Thursday.

Elected to the board were new public representative Leon E. Panetta, former chief of staff to the President and former congressman; and new industry representative David H. Komansky, chief executive of Merrill Lynch & Co Inc, the exchange said.

Panetta replaces Anthony J.F. O'Reilly, chief executive of H.J. Heinz Co, who had served three consecutive terms on the board, the maximum number of consecutive terms allowed under the NYSE constitution.
Komansky replaces Stephen L. Hammerman, chairman of Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith, Inc, who has retired from the Exchange's board, the big board said.
It said four public representatives were re-elected:
--Geoffrey C. Bible, chief executive Philip Morris Cos Inc
--J. Gary Burkhead, vice chairman, FMR Corp.
--Bernard Marcus, chief executive of Home Depot Inc
--Kathryn J. Whitmire, director, National Resource Center for Public Leadership, University of Maryland
The exchange said five securities-industry representatives were re-elected:
--Charles J. Bocklet, Jr., managing partner, Bocklet & Co LP
--Michel A. David-Weill, chairman, Lazard Freres & Co LLC
--Robert B. Fagenson, president, Fagenson & Co Inc
--Richard B. Fisher, chairman, Morgan Stanley Group Inc.
--Benjamin H. Griswold IV, chairman, Alex. Brown Inc's Alex. Brown & Sons Inc
Re-elected as vice chairmen of the board were, James A. Jacobson, senior managing member, Benjamin Jacobson & Sons LLC, and Deryck C. Maughan, chief executive of Salomon Inc's Salomon Brothers Inc.

In addition to the 11 directors elected or re-elected to the board today, the board will be seeking the nominating committee's recommendation for a replacement for a 12th nominee, who would fill the vacancy left by director Paul A. Allaire, chief executive of Xerox Corp, who withdrew after being nominated for re-election.
The nominating committee is composed of eight members: four public representatives and four from the securities industry, the exchange said.
The committee is independent of the board.
The nominations are not approved by the board before being submitted to the membership for voting.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
